title: Spark's governance process is written against a Powerhouse system that does not yet exist, with signed forum posts as the fallback
content:
Two paired provisions concede that the canonical rails are not built yet. A.6.1.1.1.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.1.2 states that "until the Powerhouse system supports submitting Artifact Edit Proposals," holders may submit by posting to the Sky Forum under "Spark Prime" with a title containing "Spark Artifact Edit Proposal" and "cryptographic proof that the author controls an account holding the required percentage of the total SPK token supply." A.6.1.1.1.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.5.1 adds that until Powerhouse supports updating Artifacts, the Operational Facilitator works with the Core Facilitator to update the Atlas GitHub repository to reflect approved proposals.

The pattern is that the *rule* is specified at its intended end state while an explicitly labelled Short-Term Transitionary Measure supplies a manual equivalent. The requirement being satisfied — proof of eligible stake, and a durable record of the approved edit — stays constant; only the mechanism degrades.

What the fallback costs is verifiability. On the intended rails, eligibility and edit provenance are machine-checkable. In the interim, eligibility rests on a signature posted to a forum and evaluated by the Facilitator, and the authoritative text of the Artifact is a git history maintained by two facilitators.

This is worth reading as a general caution for Atlas provisions: a process described in system terms may currently be executing as a human procedure, and the trust assumptions of the two differ.
description: Until tooling ships, proposals are Sky Forum posts carrying cryptographic proof of holdings and approved edits land as GitHub pull requests against the Atlas repository.
